sources.entry: motion-skills by iart.ai - An open-source collection of ~50 motion-graphics, animation, and video skills across 14 installable packs — kinetic typography, data-driven charts, explainers, TikTok/Reels, web/WebGL animation, and Manim math animation — that teach an agent how a professional would build each piece. Every visual skill ships a deliver-and-verify loop (render a frame → screenshot → check)

summary.one_liner: A collection of about 56 open-source skill folders (SKILL.md plus references) that teach AI coding agents how to build motion graphics, animation, and video, grouped into 19 installable packs.
use_cases: Teach a coding agent to build kinetic typography or title animations
Generate animated data charts from a CSV
Produce vertical short-form videos for TikTok, Reels, or Shorts
Create math explainer animations with Manim
Build web and WebGL animations in HTML
Make transparent lower thirds for streaming overlays
notable: Each visual skill includes a deliver-and-verify loop: render a frame, screenshot it, and check the result
Split into 19 installable packs, each for a different audience, so users install only what they need
Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and 40+ agents via npx skills or a Claude Code plugin marketplace
No model fine-tuning or plugin runtime; skills are plain markdown know-how with a scripts/ toolkit for freezing frames, contact sheets, and MP4 probing
caveats: The README describes the packs as the open-source craft behind iart.ai, a commercial AI motion agent that the README promotes as an alternative to running the skills yourself
Video skills depend on Remotion or Manim, which need their own setup; the README does not detail those steps
README does not state a version or maintenance status
